# Test Case Rule: RULE 121: In harts without additional user extensions requiring new state, the XS field in mstatus is read-only zero.
##### ASSEMBLY #####
li t0, 0x18000
csrrs x0, mstatus, t0
csrr a0, mstatus
and a0, a0, t0
# Result: a0 = 0

# Test Case Rule: RULE 122: Changing the setting of the FS field in mstatus has no effect on the contents of the floating-point register state.
##### ASSEMBLY #####
li t0, 0x6000
csrrs x0, mstatus, t0
li a0, 0x0123456789abcdef
fmv.d.x f0, a0
csrrc x0, mstatus, t0
li t0, 0x4000
csrrs x0, mstatus, t0
fmv.x.d a0, f0
# Result: a0 = 0x0123456789abcdef

# Test Case Rule: RULE 123: Setting the FS field in mstatus to Off does not destroy the floating-point state, and setting the FS field to Initial does not clear the floating-point contents.
##### ASSEMBLY #####
li t0, 0x6000
csrrs x0, mstatus, t0
li a0, 0x0123456789abcdef
fmv.d.x f0, a0
csrrc x0, mstatus, t0
li t0, 0x2000
csrrs x0, mstatus, t0
fmv.x.d a0, f0
# Result: a0 = 0x0123456789abcdef

# Test Case Rule: RULE 124: Changing the setting of the VS field in mstatus has no effect on the contents of the vector register state.
##### ASSEMBLY #####
li t0, 0x600
csrrs x0, mstatus, t0
vsetivli zero, 1, e8, m1, ta, ma
csrw vstart, x0
li a0, 0x5a
vmv.s.x v1, a0
csrrc x0, mstatus, t0
li t0, 0x200
csrrs x0, mstatus, t0
vmv.x.s a0, v1
# Result: a0 = 0x5a

# Test Case Rule: RULE 125: The FS field in mstatus is set directly by privileged code when resuming a user context, while the XS field in mstatus is set indirectly by writing to the status register of the individual extensions.
##### ASSEMBLY #####
nop # Skipped because no individual extension status register is specified
# Result: x0 = 0

# Test Case Rule: RULE 126: Machine mode and Supervisor mode share a single copy of the FS, VS, and XS bits in mstatus.
##### ASSEMBLY #####
li t0, 0x6600
csrrc x0, mstatus, t0
li t0, 0x4200
csrrs x0, mstatus, t0
call machine_to_supervisor
csrr a0, sstatus
li t0, 0x6600
and a0, a0, t0
# Result: a0 = 0x4200

# Test Case Rule: RULE 127: The SD bit in mstatus is read-only and is set when either the FS, VS, or XS bits in mstatus encode a Dirty state (i.e., SD = (FS==0b11 OR VS==0b11 OR XS==0b11)).
##### ASSEMBLY #####
li t0, 0x6000
csrrs x0, mstatus, t0
li t1, 1 << 63
csrrc x0, mstatus, t1
csrr a0, mstatus
srli a0, a0, 63
# Result: a0 = 1

# Test Case Rule: RULE 128: In mstatus, the encoding 0 for FS and VS means Off, 1 means Initial, 2 means Clean, and 3 means Dirty.
##### ASSEMBLY #####
li t0, 0x6600
csrrc x0, mstatus, t0
li t1, 0x6400
csrrs x0, mstatus, t1
csrr a0, mstatus
and a0, a0, t0
# Result: a0 = 0x6400

# Test Case Rule: RULE 129: In mstatus, the encoding 0 for XS means All off, 1 means None dirty or clean with some on, 2 means None dirty with some clean, and 3 means Some dirty.
##### ASSEMBLY #####
nop # Skipped because no individual extension state contributing to XS is specified
